note: Old Nettle. There is exactly one of him, he turns up perhaps five times in the life of a villager, and the whole point of this rig is that the first time you see that outline across a field you know which of those two kinds of evening you are having.

It is built for one camera. From an isometric view you see the top of a thing before you see its face, so the whole silhouette is a wide flat disc over a vertical line: a hat brim nothing else in the game has, on a body drawn thin enough to disappear behind it. At the distance where an ogre is still a lump and a villager is still a villager, that is already unmistakably him.

Every part of the hat and the head turns about [0, 1.74, 0], which is the neck. A hat that swings on a different point from the head it is on comes loose every time he looks round, so if you move one of those pivots move all of them.

parts.note: Two stalks for legs, set close together. Nothing else in the game stands on a base this narrow, and it is what makes the brim above look as wide as it does.
The coat: long, and narrow front to back so he reads as an edge rather than a body.
Shoulders as a thin plank. From above this is the only horizontal below the hat, which is what stops the brim looking like a hat floating on a stick.
And no face on it. The brim keeps the head in its own shade from every angle the camera has, so eyes would be two pixels nobody ever sees; the absence is the better answer.
Arms hung long, past the knee, and swinging from the shoulder plank.
The switch he carries, leaning out from the hand that holds it: the reach arrives before he does.
A coat tail that trails behind him, and is the only part of him that ever looks hurried.
